newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, eye possible rate rise Friday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, eye possible rate rise Friday.

text.p: Polish shares eased after a two-day gain and analysts said investors would be waiting for news from a central bank news conference at 1300 GMT.

On Wedesday the central bank president said the bank would soon raise its nominal interest rates to offset the monetary effect of flood relief credit for the government, but analysts said the bourse may already have priced in such a move.

"Everyone already knew about rates and this week was enough time to react....I think a greater influence will be whether it will be a rise of one percent or three," said Artur Kobos, a trader at ING Barings in Warsaw.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.3 percent to 15,116.8 points and turnover fell 15 percent to 156.4 million zlotys on both markets.
Analysts were surprised that Budimex, down nine percent in active trade, continued its recent plunge on news it had revised down its 1997 profit forecast.
They said Optimus, down 5.1 percent in active trade, fell after the stock's speculative surge this week.
They said top gainer Prochnik, up 9.7 percent, also continued to see speculative swings.
